sections.h2: Where do Chattooga County property taxes get paid and who sets the value?
sections.html:
Billing and collection sit with the Chattooga County Tax Commissioner, who has no say over values or millage rates. The Board of Tax Assessors, appointed by the county commissioner, appraises property and approves every exemption claimed. The Board of Equalization, appointed by the Grand Jury, hears appeals. The millage rate itself comes from the county commissioner for county tax and the Board of Education for school tax.

  • Tax Commissioner: Courthouse Annex, 120 Cox Street, Summerville, GA 30747; postal box: P.O. Box 517, Summerville, GA 30747-0517.
  • Phone 706-857-0703. Hours run 7:30 AM to 5:30 PM Monday through Friday, and the office is closed on Wednesdays.
  • Bills can be searched and paid online at chattoogacountytax.com.
  • A mailed payment is accepted with a United States Postal Service postmark, but not with a metered postmark.

Tax bills go to the homeowner and only sometimes to the mortgage company, so forward your bill to the lender if your taxes are escrowed.

sections.h2: What should a seller picture when thinking of Chattooga County?
sections.html:
Chattooga County sits in Georgia's northwest corner. It was created on December 28, 1838 and was named for the Chattooga River. It covers 314 square miles, of which 313 are land. Summerville serves as the seat, with Trion, Lyerly and Menlo as the other incorporated cities. Walker and Floyd counties lie to the north and southeast, and a corner of the Chattahoochee National Forest reaches into the county. The Summerville micropolitan area is part of the Rome-Summerville combined statistical area.

History left landmarks here. The 1863 Battle of Trion Factory was fought along present-day First Street, and the Old Trion Cemetery holds graves of soldiers killed in that fight. Several county properties carry national historic listings, which is worth knowing because Georgia offers preferential assessment for qualifying historic buildings.

Two public school systems serve the county: the Chattooga County School System and the Trion City School System. Census QuickFacts estimates 25,300 residents for 2025, close to the 24,965 counted in 2020 and below the 26,015 of 2010. On the 2020 to 2024 survey, a typical owner-held home is worth $115,600, a typical rent is $790, a typical household takes in $50,285, and 66.8% of homes are owned by their occupants. Only 2 building permits were issued in 2025, and workers average a 28.1 minute trip to the job.

sections.h2: What is the Chattooga County payment deadline, and what does paying late cost?
sections.html:
December 1 is the usual deadline for land, buildings and business equipment. Interest runs from the day following that deadline, and a 5% penalty is added once 120 days pass. A homesteaded parcel owing less than $500 escapes the 120-day penalty. Mobile and manufactured homes are due April 1, with interest of 1% added monthly if they are late.

Unpaid taxes can be levied on, though the Tax Commissioner describes that as a last resort. Once a bill is more than 30 days late, a tax fifa (lien) can be entered in the Superior Court clerk's records. Those entries are public, credit bureaus may use them, and the tax office cannot control that.

Listings of excess funds from past tax sales are posted on the Tax Commissioner's website, so a former owner can check whether money is waiting.

sections.h2: Which homestead exemptions does Chattooga County offer?
sections.html:
The Tax Commissioner lists state exemptions and local ones that replace the state amount when larger. Ownership and residence on January 1 are required, and the application goes to the Tax Assessor's Office. Filing is open all year, but only an application in hand by April 1 takes effect that year.

Homestead exemptions listed by the Chattooga County Tax Commissioner
ExemptionWho qualifiesWhat it does
StandardAny qualifying homeowner$2,000 off the 40% assessed value; excludes bond levies
Standard elderly schoolAge 62 or older, net income at most $10,000Up to $10,000 off assessed value, school tax only
Standard elderly generalAge 65 or older, net income at most $10,000Up to $4,000 off assessed value for county, school and state
Local countyAge 70 or older, federal adjusted gross income at most $20,000Sliding 20% to 100% share of assessed value, county tax only, for the residence and up to 5 acres
Local schoolAge 70 or older, same income limitUp to $40,000 of assessed value, school tax only
FloatingAge 62 or older, household income at most $30,000State and county tax, not school; replaces other exemptions

The office cautions that the floating exemption can raise a bill at first, since it replaces other state and county exemptions already in place. Service-connected disabled veterans have their own exemption, and so do unremarried widows of service members killed in armed conflict and of firefighters or peace officers who died on duty.

sections.h2: Can Chattooga County owners defer tax or get a lower assessment?
sections.html:
Owners 62 or older whose gross household income is up to $15,000 can defer, but not escape, tax on a homestead. The deferred amount generally stays due until ownership changes or the deferred taxes plus interest reach 85% of fair market value, which means a sale usually triggers repayment from proceeds.

  • Agricultural land used in bona fide farming can be assessed at 30% instead of 40%, and conservation use property is valued at its current use. Both require a covenant to keep the use for at least 10 years.
  • Qualifying historic buildings can receive preferential assessment on the structure and up to two acres around it.
  • Manufacturers can claim the Freeport exemption on raw goods, goods in process and finished goods awaiting out-of-state shipment, by applying with the Board of Tax Assessors between January 1 and April 1.

sections.h2: What is the route for contesting a Chattooga County value?
sections.html:
The deadline to contest is 45 days after the notice date. Your appeal lands first with the assessors, who look at their value again. If you remain unhappy, the next stop is the Board of Equalization or an arbitrator, and a final written notice sent or filed with the assessors carries the case to Superior Court.

Grounds for an appeal are taxability, value, or uniformity compared with neighboring properties. A complaint that the tax is too high does not qualify, since the county commissioner and Board of Education set that. Mobile home owners who dispute a revised value have 30 days to reach the Board of Equalization.

Returns are accepted until April 1. After a first return, real property returns carry forward unless something changes, but personal property returns are needed every year.

sections.h2: What tax points matter when selling in Chattooga County?
sections.html:
Whoever holds title on January 1 owes tax for the full year, and state revenue guidance confirms there is no refund for part-year owners. A closing attorney should divide the year on the settlement statement.

Your exemption stays behind with you, and a purchaser moving in must file by April 1. If you need a copy of a deed for the closing file, the Clerk of Superior Court keeps a deed room in the Chattooga County Courthouse. Because property in this county is lower priced than the other three Georgia counties compared on QuickFacts, even a modest unpaid balance and penalty can matter to a sale, so pull a payoff early.

faqs.q: What is the usual Chattooga County deadline?
faqs.a: December 1 for land, buildings and business equipment. Mobile and manufactured homes run on an April 1 schedule.

faqs.q: Can I visit the Chattooga tax office on a Wednesday?
faqs.a: No. The Tax Commissioner's office is closed on Wednesdays and open 7:30 AM to 5:30 PM the other weekdays.

faqs.q: How costly is a late payment in Chattooga County?
faqs.a: Interest starts the day after the due date. A 5% penalty applies after 120 days, except for homesteaded property with liability under $500.

faqs.q: Does a Chattooga County homestead exemption need yearly renewal?
faqs.a: No. Once granted it renews automatically unless you move, change ownership or want a different exemption, and the deadline for a first application is April 1.

faqs.q: How do I find a deed copy for a Chattooga County property?
faqs.a: Ask the Superior Court clerk, whose deed room is in the Chattooga County Courthouse.
